title: Human-facing output when stdout is a terminal
body: Humans run a small read-mostly subset (list, ready, blocked, show, log, doctor, memories; create, close, update) and agents read a pipe, so gate formatting on isatty rather than a second UI. Pain today: nanosecond RFC 3339 timestamps everywhere; 'on <branch> (<commit>)' stamps on every created/closed line; list aligns status only and nothing is colored; show leaves bodies and notes unwrapped. Do: relative or short times, aligned columns, color on status and priority, wrapped bodies, all off when piped, under NO_COLOR, or with --plain. prime always emits the plain form. Then a foam board one-screen overview (epics with rollups, ready, in progress, blocked, recent log). Revisit a TUI only if something is left that this cannot do.

notes.author: Jack Roddy
notes.text: Options weighed. (1) TTY-aware text layer: color, relative times, aligned columns, wrapped bodies, off when piped; one afternoon, one or two small crates. (2) foam board: a one-screen overview; the seed of a TUI if one is ever wanted. (3) Full TUI with ratatui: most formatting freedom, but a second product with navigation, key bindings, forms and a render loop, for a tool whose value is the agent side, and it would call the same model code the text layer needs anyway. Chosen: 1 then 2, then judge whether anything only a TUI can do remains. Who runs what: humans read (list, ready, blocked, show, log, doctor, memories) and occasionally create, close, update, config; agents run prime, claim, heartbeat, note, remember and --json, and never see a terminal because Claude Code's Bash tool, hooks and JSON callers read a pipe. Caveat: some harnesses run commands under a pseudo-terminal, so an agent could see the human format; NO_COLOR, --plain and prime always emitting plain text cover that.
